metadata.case_name: WONG KIM HUNG BY HIS NEXT FRIEND HIU SJU PHIN v. WONG WING KONG T/A 613 DECORATION WORKS AND OTHERS

injuries.description: Severe head injury with intracranial haemorrhage and multiple fractures of the skull
source: The experts are agreed that the plaintiff had severe head injury with loss of consciousness for about 4 weeks. He had intracranial haemorrhage and multiple fractures of the skull. Intracranial pressure monitoring and intensive care was required. As a result he experienced dizziness, neurocognitive and neurobehavioural impairments, mild dysarthria and weakness and clumsiness of both upper limbs and right lower limb.

injuries.description: Deep laceration of about 8 cm on forehead and multiple bruises on right chest
source: He had deep laceration of about 8 cm on his forehead and multiple bruises on his right chest.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

manifestations.description: Loss of consciousness for about 4 weeks
Weakness and clumsiness of both upper limbs and right lower limb
Mentally incapacitated person (MIP) - incapable of managing or administering his own properties and affairs

treatments_received: stayed in the intensive care unit for 3 days
remained hospitalized until he was discharged 4 months later on 14 December 2007
follow up at the neurological ward and outpatient clinic

losses.description: He has become an MIP and is wheelchair bound.
He is a MIP incapable of managing or administering his own properties and affairs; requires assistance in dressing and bathing though can perform feeding and toileting by himself.
Complete loss of earning capacity (100%); cannot continue working as a construction worker.
Neurocognitive and neurobehavioural impairments, slow response and bad memory.
Life expectancy reduced to not more than 75% of the normal population, ie 14 years from mid 2013 (Dr Woo).

comparable_cases.case_name: Hui Yiu Wing v Regional Council
comparable_cases.injury_description: Plaintiff, aged 12, sustained fracture of skull base, traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage and intracranial air; developed hyponatraemia and convulsion, with verbal and intellect impairment; 20% impairment of the whole person and another 2% for risk of epilepsy; loss of earning capacity at least 50%.

comparable_cases.case_name: Ngan Man Yuk v Lau Kwan Him
comparable_cases.injury_description: CT brain showed left acute subdural haematoma and left fronto-temporal contusion; emergency burr hole and craniotomy; subsequent epileptic attacks and severe impairment of cognitive functions, perception, memory, thinking and language; impaired speech and headaches; could not manage her own affairs.

comparable_cases.case_name: Law Ping Leung v Ng Sze Pong
comparable_cases.injury_description: Regained consciousness after about 10 days' hospitalization; contusion over right temporal region with traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage, skull base fracture, fractured right clavicle and bilateral lung contusion with pneumothorax; stayed in ICU for 2 weeks; substantial impairment of thinking process and memory; mild dysphagia and mild left hemiparesis; personality change; neurocognitive and neurobehavioural impairment making it unlikely to manage personal and financial affairs.
